title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: first knot — Vasquez: even if Christ ordered after predestination, in execution Christ's merit causes every predestination-effect; intending a sinner's salvation with means that first satisfy justice is mercy, not loving the sinner more than justice
pass_a_gloss: What therefore was objected — that the Divine justice is shaken, if we place God as having first elected certain ones unto life before he ordained Christ unto expiating sins — this scruple can be dissolved. First, if anyone with the subtle Doctor answer, Howsoever Christ and the merits of Christ toward men were ordained after predestination, yet since in execution the merit of Christ is the cause of whatsoever effect flowing from predestination, nothing is done against the justice of God in the salvation of the elect. For of mere mercy to intend the salvation of some sinner, and from this intention to provide him such media that this by no means be done before justice shall have been satisfied, is not to love the sinner more than justice, but to will to exercise gratuitous mercy toward the sinner, rather than due justice.
pass_b_english: So the objection that divine justice is shaken if we set God as electing some to life before ordaining Christ to expiate sins — that scruple can be loosed. First, with the subtle Doctor: however Christ and his merits toward men were ordered after predestination, yet in execution Christ's merit is the cause of every effect flowing from predestination — so nothing is done against God's justice in the elect's salvation. Of mere mercy to intend a sinner's salvation, and from that intention to provide him such means that it is never done before justice is satisfied, is not to love the sinner more than justice — it is to will to exercise free mercy toward the sinner rather than due justice.
source_text: Quod igitur objectum fuit, labefactari Divinam justitiam, si ponamus Deum prius elegisse quosdam ad vitam, quam ordinaverit Christum ad expianda peccata, hic scrupulus dissolvi potest. Primo, si quis cum subtili Doctore respondeat, Utcunque Christus Christique merita erga homines ordinata fuerunt post praedestinationem, tamen cum in exsecutione meritum Christi sit causa cujuscunque effectus a praedestinatione manantis, nihil fit contra justitiam Dei in salute electorum. Nam ex mera misericordia intendere salutem alicujus peccatoris, atque ex hac intentione providere illi talia media, ut hoc minime fiat priusquam justitiae fuerit satisfactum, non est peccatorem magis amare quam justitiam, sed velle exercere gratuitam misericordiam erga peccatorem, potius quam debitam justitiam.
